finding.summary: 论文要求最小 k 使累计≥γ；代码取累计>γ 的最小 k（累计恰等于 γ 时多选一条），且 //128+1 放大、min/max_budget 覆盖，K_v 不再是论文定义的最小前缀（artifact 范围：>γ 而非 ≥γ，且 //128+1 与预算截断改变前缀长度）
finding.condition: torch.any(torch.cumsum(torch.sort(vertical, dim=-1, descending=True).values, dim=-1) == gamma) or torch.any(torch.cumsum(torch.sort(slash, dim=-1, descending=True).values, dim=-1) == gamma) or torch.any(score_cover_topk(vertical, gamma) // 128 + 1 != score_cover_topk(vertical, gamma)) or torch.any(score_cover_topk(slash, gamma) // 128 + 1 != score_cover_topk(slash, gamma)) or torch.any(score_cover_topk(vertical, gamma) // 128 + 1 < min_budget) or torch.any(score_cover_topk(vertical, gamma) // 128 + 1 > max_budget) or torch.any(score_cover_topk(slash, gamma) // 128 + 1 < min_budget) or torch.any(score_cover_topk(slash, gamma) // 128 + 1 > max_budget)

analysis.reasoning: The code's score_cover_topk counts cumsum <= gamma then adds 1, so it returns the first prefix whose sum exceeds gamma (and one extra when sum equals gamma), whereas the paper defines min k with sum >= gamma. The subsequent //128+1 and min/max_budget clamps further change the prefix length. Thus the artifact deviates as claimed.
analysis.would_confirm: Run score_cover_topk on a vector whose cumulative sum equals gamma and compare returned k to the paper's min{k: cumsum>=gamma}.
